findings.claim: RANK 1 — Cross-asset trend following (Faber 10-month SMA / long-only time-series momentum on asset-class ETFs) has the strongest out-of-sample evidence for DRAWDOWN CONTROL, but essentially no evidence of beating buy-and-hold on return since ~2009. It is a drawdown-insurance sleeve, not an alpha sleeve.
findings.evidence: Century-scale: AQR 'Century of Evidence' TSMOM (1903-2012, net of simulated t-costs AND 2/20 fees) 14.3%/yr, 9.9% vol, Sharpe 1.00, positive in 9 of the 10 worst 60/40 drawdowns; but the most recent decade in their table (2003-Jun 2012) was net Sharpe 0.61, second-worst of 11 decades, and AQR's own conservative forward assumption is 0.4 net. Live long-short proxies: SG Trend +27.3% in 2022; DBMF ETF since Jun-2019: 9.1% CAGR, Sharpe 0.61, MaxDD -17.3% (2023 -9%); KMLM since 2021: 5.8%, Sharpe 0.26, MaxDD -25.9%. Long-only ETF version (my yfinance replication, 10 bps/side, monthly): SPY 10m-SMA-vs-cash 2004-2026: 8.8% CAGR, 10.3% vol, Sharpe 0.76, MaxDD -22.4% vs SPY 10.9%/14.5%/0.71/-50.8%. But 2015-2026 OOS: 7.4%/11.3%/0.52/-22.4% vs SPY 13.7%/14.9%/0.81/-23.9% — 24 of 141 months in cash, yearly shortfalls vs SPY of -5.7 (2015), -7.2 (2016), -21.0 (2019), -17.0 (2023), -10.7 (2026 YTD), and it LOST MORE than SPY in 2022 (-20.5 vs -18.2) from an exit/re-entry whipsaw. GTAA-5 equal-weight (SPY/EFA/IEF/VNQ/DBC, 10m SMA) 2007-2026: 5.3%/6.6%/0.61/-11.4%; 2015+: 5.6%/5.9%/0.63/-6.1%. findings.claim: RANK 2 — Cross-asset relative momentum WITH a per-asset trend filter (Faber 'aggressive GTAA' top-3 of 13 ETFs by average 1/3/6/12-month return, each must be above its 10-month SMA else cash) is the best return-generating sleeve available to a long-only ETF retail account, with acceptable OOS Sharpe and tolerable turnover.
findings.evidence: My replication (13 ETFs: SPY QQQ IWM EFA EEM VNQ DBC GLD IEF TLT LQD TIP AGG; 10 bps/side): 2008-2026 9.6% CAGR, 11.7% vol, Sharpe 0.73, MaxDD -17.5%, worst year -8.8% (2015); 2015+ (true OOS for the 2013 paper): 8.8%/11.1%/0.65/-17.5%; 2020+: 14.1%/11.5%/0.98/-10.1%. One-way turnover 6.7x/yr → 0.67%/yr drag at 10 bps, 1.3% at 20 bps. Failure modes observed: momentum-chasing whipsaw in 2015 (-8.8%) and 2016 (-1.5%), concentration in 3 assets, 2011-2012 flat (-0.1%, +1.0%). Year-by-year 2008+: +10.2, +17.7, +13.3, -0.1, +1.0, +25.7, +9.9, -8.8, -1.5, +18.8, -2.8, +6.6, +24.9, +17.2, -4.1, +9.0, +17.9, +23.9, +9.3(2026 YTD). findings.claim: RANK 3 — Volatility targeting is worth using ONLY as a scale-down drawdown/tail overlay (no leverage), never as a return or Sharpe enhancer; real-time implementations do not reliably beat unmanaged portfolios.
findings.evidence: Cederburg-O'Doherty-Wang-Yan (JFE 2020, 103 equity strategies): vol-managed versions show positive alphas in spanning regressions but 'reasonable out-of-sample versions generally earn lower certainty equivalent returns and Sharpe ratios than … the original, unmanaged portfolios', due to structural instability; Moreira-Muir (2017) and Harvey et al. (2018) scaling is ex post. Harvey/Man: Sharpe gains only for equities/credit, negligible for bonds/commodities/FX; consistent DD and left-tail reduction. My replication: 60/40 with 10% vol target (3m realized, cap 1x) 2003-2026: Sharpe 0.88 vs 0.85 unmanaged, MaxDD -22.6% vs -29.5%; 2015+: Sharpe 0.71 vs 0.73, MaxDD -14.7% vs -20.5%; turnover only 0.64x/yr. In the recommended mix a 10% cap trimmed vol 8.2→7.7% and CAGR 8.0→7.4% but did NOT reduce MaxDD (-11.5% either way) because the mix's worst drawdown was a slow low-vol grind (2015-16), not a crash.

findings.claim: RANK 4 — Antonacci GEM (dual momentum, 12-month lookback, SPY/ex-US/AGG) has decayed sharply since publication and is specification-fragile; usable only if ensembled across lookbacks and with cash (not bonds) as the risk-off asset.
findings.evidence: My replication (SPY/VEU(EFA)/AGG, 12m, 10 bps): 2004-2026 9.7% CAGR, 12.2% vol, Sharpe 0.73, MaxDD -19.8%; 2015+ OOS: 8.0%/12.8%/0.52/-19.8% vs SPY 13.7%/14.9%/0.81/-23.9% — i.e., lower Sharpe AND nearly the same drawdown as buy-and-hold, with worst year -17.1% (2022, because AGG was the risk-off asset). Newfound Research fragility study: 9-month vs 10-month lookback produced 43.1% vs 146.1% cumulative return over the same window; 2010: +12.2% vs -9.3% between adjacent lookbacks; style whipsaw in late-2015/early-2016 across nearly all specs; authors recommend an equal-weight ensemble of 7 lookbacks. Multiple sources document GEM lagging S&P 500 from 2014-2022.

findings.claim: RANK 5 — Low-volatility and quality tilts are persistent but delivered NO alpha and lower Sharpe than the index in 2015-2026; they are a vehicle choice for reducing beta, not a strategy sleeve.
findings.evidence: Live ETFs (yfinance, total return, no t-costs beyond ER): USMV 2015+: 10.0% CAGR, 11.8% vol, Sharpe 0.71, MaxDD -19.1%; QUAL 2015+: 13.1%/15.1%/0.77/-27.8%; SPY 13.7%/14.9%/0.81/-23.9%. S&P 500 Low Vol index underperformed the market by >30% cumulatively in 2019-2020; Blitz-van Vliet-Baltussen (2019) argue the effect is persistent but the post-2016 excess return of median low-vol strategies fell to negative by 2020. McLean-Pontiff: anomaly returns 26% lower post-sample, 58% lower post-publication.

findings.claim: RANK 6 — Cross-sectional 12-1 stock momentum (Jegadeesh-Titman) long-only top decile in large caps is not worth a custom stock engine: the long-short premium has decayed to near zero post-2015 and the long-only version is statistically indistinguishable from the market with higher vol, deeper drawdowns and ~100%+/yr turnover.
findings.evidence: Ken French data (downloaded, through 2026-07): UMD long-short annualized 8.7% Sharpe 0.54 (1927-1992, pre-publication), 10.5%/0.62 (1993-2008), -9.1%/-0.45 (2009-2014, momentum crash), 2.2%/0.16 (2015-2026), 2.1%/0.15 (2020-2026). Value-weighted top-decile 12-2 momentum LONG-ONLY, gross of costs: 2015-2026 excess return 14.1%, vol 20.3%, Sharpe 0.69 vs market 11.9%/15.5%/0.76. Live MTUM 2015+: 14.9% CAGR, 17.3% vol, Sharpe 0.78, MaxDD -30.2% vs SPY 13.7%/14.9%/0.81/-23.9%. Alpha-decay literature (arXiv 2512.11913, withdrawn for revision) finds momentum follows hyperbolic post-publication decay and remaining-alpha forecasts overshoot as factor-ETF AUM grows. If exposure is wanted, buying MTUM inside the equity core is strictly cheaper than a home-built stock screen on yfinance data.

findings.claim: RANK 7 — Unlevered risk parity is the weakest structural candidate for a long-only retail account: its live record is poor and its central failure mode (stocks and bonds falling together) materialized in 2022.
findings.evidence: RPAR ETF since Jan-2020: 4.2% CAGR, 13.3% vol, Sharpe 0.18, MaxDD -28.6% (2022: -23%, 2024: 0%). AllocateSmartly: 2022 saw 'the worst concurrent loss in US Treasuries in over 120 years' (IEF -15.6% while SPY -23.9% over 9 months), which is exactly what risk parity's bond overweight is exposed to. Harvey et al. find vol-targeting gives negligible Sharpe benefit on bonds/commodities, so risk-weighting does not rescue those sleeves. Trend-filtering the diversifiers instead (my Sleeve C: GLD/DBC/TLT/IEF equal-weight, ensemble SMA, cash when off) returned +4.8% in 2022 and +15.8% in 2008 with MaxDD -11.0% (2008+), at the cost of a low 4.3% CAGR and a flat 2012-2014.

findings.claim: RANK 8 (BOTTOM) — Residual reversal + PEAD (the prior main.py/daily_research.py design) should be dropped: PEAD is dead in the stocks a retail account can trade, and residual reversal's out-of-sample gross return does not cover its turnover cost.
findings.evidence: Martineau, 'Rest in Peace Post-Earnings Announcement Drift': prices fully reflect earnings surprises on the announcement date; PEAD gone in large caps since 2006 and recently gone in microcaps. The two 2025 rebuttal papers (Dickerson-Julliard-Mueller; Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang) find drift only in microcaps (bottom 20% by cap, ~3% of market value); excluding microcaps the t-stat falls from 2.18 to 1.43 (UCLA Anderson Review). Huij-Lansdorp 'Residual Momentum and Reversal Strategies Revisited' (US, long-short, gross): residual reversal in-sample 1986-2008 11.1%/yr, vol 9.4%, return/risk 1.18 → out-of-sample 2009-2015 3.9%/yr, vol 7.3%, 0.53; residual momentum in-sample 13.1% → OOS -0.4%/yr. A 1-month-formation reversal strategy turns over ~100%/month; at 10-20 bps/side that is 12-24 pp/yr of cost against 3.9% gross, and half the return is on the short side a long-only account cannot hold. Crowding research also finds reversal factors have 1.7-1.8x higher crash probability when crowded.

findings.claim: A concrete, non-optimized sleeve mix (40% trend-filtered equity core / 40% trend-filtered cross-asset momentum / 20% trend-filtered diversifiers, 10% vol cap, monthly) delivered roughly 60/40's Sharpe with about half its drawdown over 2008-2026 and in the 2015+ window, after 10 bps costs — but it lags SPY badly in bull markets and the Sharpe should be haircut ~30-50% going forward.

Year-by-year: 2008 +6.5, 2009 +11.7, 2010 +4.9, 2011 +2.2, 2012 +2.6, 2013 +18.7, 2014 +7.3, 2015 -6.8, 2016 +1.0, 2017 +16.8, 2018 -1.2, 2019 +8.3, 2020 +13.4, 2021 +14.6, 2022 -5.2, 2023 +7.8, 2024 +14.2, 2025 +19.3, 2026 YTD +7.2. Deflated Sharpe (Bailey-LdP) for 2015+ with the ~12 correlated variants I looked at: DSR 0.97, minimum track record for SR>0 at 95% = 73 months — BUT the design used hindsight (2022 taught 'defensive assets need momentum too'), so treat 2015+ as only partly out-of-sample. Ensemble SMA (6/8/10/12) for the equity core beat single 10m SMA and the dual SMA+12m signal in Sharpe (0.73 vs 0.64 vs 0.61, 2008+) and MaxDD (-13.3 vs -16.2), consistent with Newfound/Zakamulin's warnings about single-parameter fragility.

findings.claim: Transaction-cost assumptions of 10-20 bps one-way are realistic on Alpaca for this universe; commodity/EM ETFs sit at the high end.
findings.evidence: Alpaca: commission-free for US-listed stocks/ETFs; fractional shares are market-orders-only during regular hours; 'cls' time-in-force gives MOC/LOC for whole shares (rejected after 15:50 ET). Spreads: SPY ~0.3 bp, GLD 4-7 bp, broad equity ETFs typically 1-3 cents/share; commodity ETPs average >0.5% spread class-wide, so DBC/EEM/VNQ should be modeled at 15-20 bps and SPY/IEF/TLT/AGG/GLD/QQQ at 5-10 bps. AQR's own 2003-2012 one-way cost assumptions for futures were 6 bp equities, 1 bp bonds, 10 bp commodities.

findings.claim: Post-publication decay is the base rate, not the exception: expect roughly half of any published in-sample edge to survive, and less for mechanical short-horizon factors.
findings.evidence: McLean-Pontiff (JF 2016, 97 predictors): returns 26% lower out-of-sample, 58% lower post-publication. Replications put the median OOS/in-sample Sharpe ratio at ~0.55-0.57. Zakamulin (2013/2017) shows moving-average timing results are 'contaminated by data-mining' and that the majority of tested rules fail out of sample. This is why every expected-return figure in this report is stated after a 30-50% haircut to the replication numbers.

findings.claim: Newer 'canary' TAA strategies (Keller HAA/BAA/VAA) show good since-publication numbers but carry more parameters and known overfitting risk; not recommended as a core sleeve for a first version.
findings.evidence: HAA (published Feb 2023): 2024 +17.3% with -2.1% DD, 2025 YTD +3.0% (third-party tracking). AllocateSmartly flags that real TIPS data only exist from 1997 (canary asset is simulated before that), that the TIPS indicator 'has been less effective than average over the last decade', 54% of gains are short-term, and the authors themselves acknowledge 'potential for unintentional overfitting'. Only ~3.5 years of live data.

recommendations: Replace the residual-reversal + PEAD stock engine entirely with an ETF-only multi-asset trend/momentum engine. Nothing in the 2015-2026 evidence supports stock-level PEAD or 1-month reversal for a long-only retail account after costs.

Sleeve mix (all long-only, cash = BIL or SGOV, never AGG/IEF as the default risk-off asset): (A) 40% trend-filtered equity core: SPY 2/3 + EFA 1/3 (or VTI/VXUS), exposure per asset = fraction of {6,8,10,12}-month SMA rules that are 'on' (0, 25, 50, 75, 100%), remainder to BIL. (B) 40% cross-asset momentum rotation: universe SPY QQQ IWM EFA EEM VNQ DBC GLD IEF TLT LQD TIP AGG; score = mean of 1/3/6/12-month total return; hold top 3 at 1/3 each ONLY if each is above its own 10-month SMA, else that third goes to BIL. (C) 20% trend-filtered diversifiers: GLD DBC TLT IEF at 5% each, same ensemble-SMA on/off rule as (A), off → BIL.

Overlay: portfolio-level volatility cap of 10% annualized (trailing 3-month realized vol of the composite; scale ALL risk weights by min(1, 10%/vol); never above 1.0, no leverage). Purpose is tail-trimming in fast crashes; do not expect it to improve Sharpe or the slow-grind drawdowns.

Cadence: monthly. Compute signals from the last trading day's close (yfinance auto_adjust), execute at the next session's open (~09:35 ET market orders; fractional notional orders for the remainder). Trade a position only if |target - current| > 4% of equity (tolerance band). No intramonth signal changes; a weekly Claude session only checks health, vol cap, kill switch and reconciliation.

Cost model in the engine and every report: 10 bps/side for SPY QQQ IWM IEF TLT AGG LQD TIP GLD BIL, 20 bps/side for DBC EEM VNQ EFA; measure realized implementation shortfall vs prior close and report it monthly. Expected turnover ~3.5-4x one-way/yr → 0.4-0.8%/yr drag.

Publish these as the HONEST expected numbers (after costs, after a 30-50% Sharpe haircut to the replication): CAGR 5-8%, vol 7-9%, Sharpe 0.4-0.6, max drawdown -15 to -20% (assume ~1.5x the backtest's -11.5%), worst calendar year -8 to -12%, underwater stretches of 2-3 years, and a high probability (>60% of rolling 3-year windows) of trailing a 60/40 benchmark during equity bull markets by up to 40 pp cumulative. The deliverable is drawdown durability, not headline returns; benchmark against 60/40 (SPY/IEF) and SPY, and report both.

Bound Claude's 'adaptation' to a pre-registered parameter set: SMA ensemble members ∈ {6,8,10,12} (never a single lookback), momentum lookbacks fixed at {1,3,6,12}, top-N ∈ {3,4}, vol cap ∈ [8%,12%], tolerance band ∈ [2%,5%], with a 6-month cooling period between changes and a written reason logged. Adding any new signal requires a pre-registered walk-forward test on data not used to design it. Never let Claude override an individual order; it can only halt (kill switch) or confirm the deterministic engine's proposed basket.

Per-strategy expected performance to encode in docs (after costs): Trend equity core: CAGR 6-8%, vol 9-10%, Sharpe 0.5-0.65, MaxDD -13 to -20%, turnover ~1.8x, fails in V-shaped corrections and shallow-correction bull runs (2019: -21 pp vs SPY; 2023: -17 pp). Cross-asset momentum rotation: CAGR 8-11%, vol 11-12%, Sharpe 0.55-0.75, MaxDD -18 to -25%, turnover ~6.7x, fails in choppy multi-asset reversals (2015: -9%) and concentrates in 3 assets. Trend diversifiers: CAGR 3-6%, vol 5-6%, Sharpe 0.4-0.5, MaxDD -7 to -12%, turnover ~2.2x, dead money for multi-year stretches (2012-2014). Vol cap: -0.5 pt vol, -0.5 pt CAGR, DD reduction only in fast crashes. GEM: 7-9% CAGR, Sharpe ~0.5, MaxDD ~-20%; only as an ensembled variant with cash risk-off. Long-only stock momentum: ≈ market Sharpe, +2-3 pt vol, deeper DD — if wanted, hold MTUM inside sleeve A rather than screening stocks. Low-vol/quality: no alpha; optional swap of USMV for part of SPY to cut beta. Risk parity: avoid unlevered. PEAD/reversal: avoid.

Build the research harness before the engine: keep the replication scripts (scratchpad bt.py / mix2.py, copy into /Users/prn/claude_portfolio/scripts/research/), snapshot yfinance monthly closes to state/ so historical adjusted prices cannot silently change, and add a walk-forward report (rolling 36-month Sharpe/DD vs 60/40 and SPY, deflated Sharpe, minimum track-record length) that every Claude session must regenerate before proposing any parameter change.

Preflight design (given the 401 on Alpaca keys): the engine should produce the full target basket and diff from yfinance data alone (DRY-RUN), then a separate executor step reads Alpaca positions; if Alpaca auth fails, the session reports 'keys invalid' and stores the intended basket so the next successful run is idempotent (client_order_id = hash of date+ticker+target).
caveats: All replication numbers come from monthly yfinance auto-adjusted ETF closes (2003/2004-2026-09), signals computed and executed at the same month-end close, 10 bps/side flat, BIL as cash from 2007 (0% before). Real execution at next open adds overnight gap risk and slippage; commodity/EM ETF costs are higher than 10 bps. No taxes modeled (irrelevant for paper).

The 2015-2026 'out-of-sample' window is only ~11.7 years and one macro regime (US mega-cap bull with two sharp shocks). The recommended sleeve mix was assembled with knowledge of 2022 (cash-not-bonds risk-off, trend-filtered diversifiers), so its 2015+ statistics are partly in-sample; the deflated Sharpe of 0.97 counts only the ~12 variants I ran and understates the true search across the literature.

Several primary pages returned HTTP 403/404 (AllocateSmartly GEM page, Alpha Architect trend and vol-managed articles, Antonacci's Medium post, SSRN vol-targeting page); their numbers are represented via my own replications, abstracts, or secondary summaries. Faber 2013-update figures are from a secondary summary (7circles) and are approximate.
Ken French momentum data run through 2026-07; the 10-decile long-only figures are gross of transaction costs and use CRSP breakpoints, not an implementable 50-stock universe.

The vol-cap overlay did not reduce the mix's maximum drawdown in the backtest (the worst DD was a slow, low-volatility grind in 2015-2016). Do not present vol targeting as drawdown insurance against that failure mode.

Trend filters lost MORE than buy-and-hold in 2022 on SPY alone (-20.5% vs -18.2%) due to whipsaw; drawdown control comes from the multi-asset structure and cash risk-off, not from any single filter. Expect the system to look bad for multi-year stretches in equity bull markets — this is the insurance premium, and it is the most likely reason the user abandons the system.

yfinance adjusted prices can be revised retroactively (dividend adjustments, data fixes), which can change historical signals; snapshot data in state/ and reconcile signals against the stored snapshot.

code_snippets.purpose: Exact signal rules used in the replication (month-end closes m, monthly returns r). These are the rules the deterministic engine should implement; parameters are the published defaults, not tuned.
code_snippets.code:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
# m: DataFrame of month-end adjusted closes; r = m.pct_change(); rf = r['BIL'].fillna(0)

def sma_on(m, tk, n):
    return (m[tk] > m[tk].rolling(n).mean()).astype(float)

def ens_on(m, tk, ns=(6, 8, 10, 12)):          # fraction of SMA rules that are on -> 0/.25/.5/.75/1
    return sum(sma_on(m, tk, n) for n in ns) / len(ns)

# Sleeve A (40%): trend-filtered equity core, cash remainder -> BIL
A = pd.DataFrame({'SPY': ens_on(m, 'SPY') * (2/3), 'EFA': ens_on(m, 'EFA') * (1/3)})

# Sleeve B (40%): cross-asset momentum rotation with per-asset 10m SMA gate
uni = ['SPY','QQQ','IWM','EFA','EEM','VNQ','DBC','GLD','IEF','TLT','LQD','TIP','AGG']
mom = sum(m[uni].pct_change(k) for k in (1, 3, 6, 12)) / 4
above = m[uni] > m[uni].rolling(10).mean()
B = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=m.index, columns=uni)
for dt in m.index:
    row = mom.loc[dt].dropna()
    if len(row) < 8: continue
    for tk in row.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3]:
        if above.loc[dt, tk]: B.loc[dt, tk] = 1/3        # else that third stays in BIL

# Sleeve C (20%): trend-filtered diversifiers
C = pd.DataFrame({tk: ens_on(m, tk) * 0.25 for tk in ['GLD','DBC','TLT','IEF']})

# Composite target weights (decided at month-end t, held through t+1)
W = (0.4*A).reindex(columns=uni, fill_value=0).fillna(0) + 0.4*B + (0.2*C).reindex(columns=uni, fill_value=0).fillna(0)

# Vol cap: scale-down only, trailing 3m realized vol of the composite's own gross return
Wl = W.shift(1).fillna(0)
gross = (Wl * r[uni].fillna(0)).sum(axis=1) + (1 - Wl.sum(axis=1)).clip(lower=0) * rf
scale = (0.10 / (gross.rolling(3).std() * np.sqrt(12))).clip(upper=1.0).fillna(1.0)
W_target = W.mul(scale, axis=0)              # cash = 1 - W_target.sum(axis=1) -> BIL

# Cost accounting used in all reported numbers: one-way turnover x per-ticker cost
turnover = (W_target - W_target.shift(1)).abs().sum(axis=1)
net = gross - 0.0010 * turnover.shift(1).fillna(0)   # 10 bps/side; use 20 bps for DBC/EEM/VNQ/EFA in production
